title: Ancient Merv
summary: Merv is the ruin field of an oasis city on the Silk Route in Turkmenistan, with monuments visible especially from the last two millennia. UNESCO says its remains span four thousand years, while a Turkmen government account says the city itself rose around the 7th century BC.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 7th century BC when, according to the Turkmen government article, Merv rose at the site of Erk Kala (first year of that century in astronomical numbering, -699). UNESCO says the oasis remains span 4,000 years, so human use is older. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: Merv rose about the VII century BC

when.display: City from the 7th century BC; oasis settled over 4,000 years; ruins stand today

where.modern_name: State Historical and Cultural Park "Ancient Merv", Mary Region, Turkmenistan
where.historical_name: Merv, oasis city on the Silk Route

importance.justification: UNESCO calls it the oldest and best-preserved of the oasis cities on the Silk Route in Central Asia.
